n1acc8060eec.s: As originally adopted, what did the Constitution of India provide about political parties?
o: No specific provision on political parties
n1acc8060eec.x: The Constitution, as adopted, said nothing specifically about political parties.

nde5694e3ed6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about coalition politics in India?
o: It gives a single party absolute power
It may slow decision-making and cause policy reversals
Compromises can dilute strong policy measures
nde5694e3ed6.x: In coalition politics no single party has absolute power; consensus, slow decisions and diluted measures are its known effects.

nindian-polity-54-9.s: The 'Congress System' in India referred to:
o: A two-party system of Congress and one rival
A single-party State with no opposition parties
One-party dominance within a competitive multi-party democracy
A coalition of equal national parties
nindian-polity-54-9.x: The 'Congress system' meant the Congress dominating a democratic, multi-party electoral landscape after independence.

n3f5eea0f8bd.s: Who wrote 'Party Building in a New Nation'?
n3f5eea0f8bd.x: Myron Weiner wrote Party Building in a New Nation; Rajni Kothari coined the 'Congress system'.

ne6fc0d311c4.s: In Andhra Pradesh's current coalition arrangement, the BJP is:
o: A supporting partner of a dominant regional party
In opposition to the ruling coalition
ne6fc0d311c4.x: AP has a coalition in which a regional party is the dominant partner and the BJP supports it.

n2719dd1ef08.s: Which of the following is a cause of the rise of regional parties in India?
o: Uniform economic development across all regions
Decline of linguistic and caste identities
National parties fully accommodating State leaders
n2719dd1ef08.x: Regional economic neglect, not uniform development, fuels regional parties.

n1b4e19537c1.s: In which year was the Shiromani Akali Dal founded?
n1b4e19537c1.x: The Shiromani Akali Dal was founded in Punjab in 1920; 1985 is the founding year of the Asom Gana Parishad.

ne42b1e56c54.s: Which of the following may form a basis for the Election Commission to deregister a political party?
o: Failing to win any Lok Sabha seat
ne42b1e56c54.x: The ECI's deregistration power is limited and arises in cases such as fraud or ceasing allegiance to the Constitution.

n3435cb4149e.s: Under paragraph 6B of the Symbols Order, a party recognised as a State party in how many States qualifies as a National Party?
n3435cb4149e.x: Recognition as a State party in four or more States is one valid route to National Party status.

new.s: Which party formed the first non-Congress government at the Centre in 1977?
new.x: The Janata Party, a merger of Congress (O), Jana Sangh, BLD and Socialists, formed the 1977 government under Morarji Desai.

new.s: In which year was the first non-Congress government formed at the Centre?
new.x: The Janata government of 1977 was the first non-Congress government; 1989 began the multi-party coalition era.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Janata government of 1977:
1. Morarji Desai was its Prime Minister.
2. It held office from 1977 to 1979.
3. It depended on outside support as it lacked a Lok Sabha majority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Janata government (1977-79) under Morarji Desai had its own Lok Sabha majority, so statement 3 is wrong.

new.s: The National Front government of V.P. Singh (1989-90) survived with the outside support of:
o: Both the BJP and the Left
new.x: The minority National Front government had outside support of both the BJP and the Left.

new.s: The BJP government led by A.B. Vajpayee in 1996 lasted for:
new.x: Vajpayee's 1996 BJP government lasted only 13 days.

new.s: The Chandra Shekhar government (1990-91) depended on the outside support of the:
new.x: Chandra Shekhar's Samajwadi Janata Party government survived on Congress support from outside.

new.s: The UPA coalition of 2004 governed on the basis of the:
new.x: The UPA adopted the National Common Minimum Programme (2004); the National Agenda for Governance was the NDA's.

new.s: Besides a common programme, coalition partners at the Centre coordinated through a:
new.x: The coalition mechanism was a common minimum programme plus a coordination committee of partners.

new.s: In the 9th Lok Sabha (1989), the largest party, which sat in opposition, was:
new.x: In 1989 the Congress won 197 seats and was the largest party but sat in opposition; JD had 143 and BJP 85.

new.s: How many seats did the BJP win in the 13th Lok Sabha election (1999)?
new.x: The BJP won 182 seats in 1999; 161 was its 1996 tally and 138 its 2004 tally.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 14th Lok Sabha election (2004):
1. The Congress won 145 seats.
2. The BJP won 133 seats.
3. The CPI(M) won 43 seats.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: In 2004 the Congress won 145, the BJP 138 (not 133) and the CPI(M) 43 seats.

new.s: After the 1967 elections, which opposition-ruled State was the exception to coalition rule, being governed by the DMK alone?
new.x: After 1967 almost every opposition-ruled State had a coalition; Tamil Nadu, under the DMK alone, was the exception.

new.s: The coalition governments formed in several States after the 1967 elections were known as:
new.x: After losing several States in 1967, the Congress gave way to Samyukta Vidhayak Dal coalitions.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of coalition politics in India?
o: No single party held absolute power
Regional parties gained a voice in national policy
new.x: Coalition politics ended one-party dominance, but India did not become a two-party system.

new.s: Who described Congress dominance as 'dominance co-existing with competition, without a trace of alternative'?
new.x: W.H. Morris-Jones gave this description; Rajni Kothari coined the 'Congress system'.

new.s: Political parties entered the Constitution of India through the Tenth Schedule added by the:
new.x: The original Constitution was silent on parties; they entered via the Tenth Schedule added by the 52nd Amendment (1985).

new.s: The YSR Congress Party was founded by Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy in:
new.x: The YSRCP was founded in March 2011 after a split from the Congress.

new.s: Who founded the Lok Satta Party in 2006?
new.x: Jayaprakash Narayan founded the Lok Satta Party in 2006.

new.s: The Mahajana Socialist Party was founded by:
new.x: The MRPS leader Manda Krishna Madiga founded the Mahajana Socialist Party.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Praja Rajyam Party:
1. Chiranjeevi founded it at Tirupati in August 2008.
2. It won 18 seats in the 2009 Andhra Pradesh election.
3. It merged with the Telugu Desam Party in 2011.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Praja Rajyam merged with the Congress, not the TDP, in 2011; statements 1 and 2 are correct.

new.s: Within how long of its founding did the TDP win power in the January 1983 Assembly election?
new.x: Founded in 1982, the TDP won power within nine months, in January 1983.

new.s: How many seats did the TDP win in the 8th Lok Sabha (1984) to become the main opposition party?
new.x: With 30 seats the TDP became the first regional party to be the main opposition in the Lok Sabha.

new.s: In which year did continuous Congress rule in Andhra Pradesh end?
new.x: The January 1983 election ended Congress rule; 1982 is the TDP's founding year.

new.s: The 1983 Andhra Pradesh election ended Congress's unbroken rule that had continued since:
new.x: The 1983 TDP victory ended Congress rule that had lasted since the State's formation in 1956.

new.s:
Arrange the following parties in the chronological order of their founding:
1. Telugu Desam Party
2. Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam
3. Samajwadi Party
4. Bahujan Samaj Party
new.x: DMK (1949), TDP (1982), BSP (1984) and SP (1992) - the order keyed in the APPSC Group 2 Mains 2025.

new.s: Which of the following regional parties was founded earliest?
new.x: The Akali Dal (1920) is older than the DMK (1949), Shiv Sena (1966) and AGP (1985).

new.s: The Rajamannar Committee on Centre-State relations (1969) was set up by the government of:
new.x: The DMK government of Tamil Nadu under M. Karunanidhi set up the Rajamannar Committee in 1969.

new.s: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution (1973) seeking more autonomy for Punjab was adopted by the:
new.x: The Shiromani Akali Dal adopted the Anandpur Sahib Resolution in October 1973.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution came in October 1973; the Rajamannar Committee was a State-level DMK initiative that reported in 1971.

new.s: Which of the following is a National Party?
new.x: The NPP is one of the six national parties; the SP, TDP and DMK are State parties.

new.s: In 2024, the BJP defeated which regional party in Odisha?
new.x: The BJP defeated the BJD in Odisha in 2024.

new.s: The AIADMK was founded in 1972 by:
new.x: M.G. Ramachandran founded the AIADMK in 1972; Annadurai founded the DMK.

new.s: The Jannayak Janta Party, founded by Dushyant Chautala in 2018, is based in:
new.x: The JJP is a Haryana party founded by Dushyant Chautala in 2018.

new.s: Simultaneous elections, now proposed as 'One Nation, One Election', were held in the first four general elections, the last being in:
new.x: The first four general elections (1951-52, 1957, 1962 and 1967) were simultaneous.

new.s: In the Sadiq Ali case (1971), a split dispute over a party's name and symbol was decided by the:
o: Vote share in the last election
Decision of the Lok Sabha Speaker
new.x: Sadiq Ali laid down the majority-support test for split disputes under Para 15.

new.s: Under the Symbols Order, a reserved symbol such as the Lotus is available only to:
new.x: Reserved symbols belong to recognised parties; free symbols are for RUPPs and independents.

new.s: The list of free symbols notified in May 2025 contains how many symbols?
new.x: The May 2025 notification lists 184 free symbols.

new.s: A registered unrecognised party may get a common symbol if it contests at least ____ Lok Sabha seats or 5% of Assembly seats.
new.x: A RUPP gets a common symbol if it contests 2 Lok Sabha seats or 5% of Assembly seats.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about election symbols:
1. Two recognised parties in different States may hold the same reserved symbol.
2. Free symbols are meant for recognised State parties.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Recognised parties in different States may share a reserved symbol; free symbols are for RUPPs and independents.

new.s: A recognised political party may name up to how many star campaigners?
new.x: A recognised party may have up to 40 star campaigners; a RUPP only 20.

new.s: One State-party route requires 3% of Assembly seats or ____ seats, whichever is more.
new.x: The seat route is 3% of Assembly seats or 3 seats, whichever is more.

new.s: A party with 6% of valid votes in the Lok Sabha election from a State becomes a State party if it also wins:
o: 2 Assembly seats in the Lok Sabha poll
new.x: Route 2 needs 6% of Lok Sabha votes plus 1 Lok Sabha seat from the State.

new.s: As per the APPSC 2019 key, how many national parties were there in May 2020?
new.x: In May 2020 there were eight national parties; there are six now.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a national party at present?
new.x: The CPI lost national status in the April 2023 review; AAP, NPP and BSP are national parties.

new.s: A new political party must apply for registration under Section 29A within how many days of its formation?
new.x: Under Sec. 29A, RPA 1951, a party applies within 30 days of formation.

new.s: Recognised political parties get free broadcast time on:
new.x: Recognised parties get broadcast time on Akashvani and Doordarshan.
